The browning reaction named after Louis-Camille Maillard, who described it in 1912.

## What reacts

Amino acids and reducing sugars combine and break down into hundreds of flavour and colour compounds. It is a different process from caramelisation, which involves sugar alone.

## Why it needs a dry surface

The reaction becomes fast at around 140 to 165 degrees Celsius. A wet surface stays near 100 degrees while its water evaporates, so a crust only browns after the surface dries.

## What I said reading it

Crust is a drying problem first and a heat problem second.
